caption: A soccer ball rolled across a paved yard hits an empty plastic bucket standing in its path; the bucket is knocked over and the ball rolls on more slowly.

sa.check: A soccer ball rolls across a paved yard.
An empty plastic bucket stands in its path and the ball reaches it.
The ball rolls on more slowly.
The bucket is empty and standing upright before the contact.
The ball arrives first, then the bucket topples.

pc.expect: The bucket starts to move at the moment the ball reaches it and not before.
pc.fail: The bucket topples before the ball arrives; or the ball reaches the bucket and the bucket stays standing; or the ball stops short of the bucket and it falls over anyway.

pc.expect: The bucket is knocked away from the ball, the way the ball was travelling, and the ball slows at the contact while carrying on roughly the same way or stopping.
pc.fail: The bucket topples toward the ball, against its direction of travel; or the ball gathers speed after the contact; or the ball rebounds off the light empty bucket quicker than it arrived.

pc.expect: The ball and the bucket stay outside one another and above the paving.
pc.fail: The ball passes through the bucket; or the bucket sinks into the paving; or the ball passes through the ground.

pc.expect: The empty bucket is light and stiff: it tips, skids and clatters on the paving rather than folding or flying apart.
pc.fail: The bucket crumples like paper where the ball hits it; or it breaks into pieces at the contact; or it stays put as though bolted down while the ball bounces off it.

pc.expect: One ball and one bucket are there throughout.
pc.fail: The bucket vanishes as it is struck or a second one appears; or the ball vanishes after the contact; or the bucket turns into another object as it topples.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The ball's panels, the bucket's colour and the yard stay the same.
pc.fail: The ball changes colour at the contact; or the bucket changes colour or size between frames; or the paving pattern of the yard changes.
